baseline.reason: The same Docker reproducer triggered a sanitizer or race report only after introduction.; meta.json/discussion.md describe GH-13521 introducing a cron-based client->argv release: clientsCronFreeArgvIfIdle() frees argv and zeroes argv_len whenever c->argc==0 and the client has been idle 2s, without checking c->multibulklen, so a client that sent only a multibulk header (args still pending) is wrongly treated as idle. The upstream fix (08d714d0e5d5) adds the multibulklen check (confirmed present in post_benign's clientsCronFreeArgvIfIdle: "if (!c->argv || c->multibulklen || c->argc) return 0;") and also fixes argv_len bookkeeping. I built pre_intro (cf838038, which predates the cron-argv-free feature entirely -- it has no clientsCronFreeArgvIfIdle function at all), post_intro (701f0665, the buggy version), and post_benign (base + the fix patch applied, confirmed by grepping server.c) with sanitizers in Docker. I wrote a run.sh that launches redis-server in the background, waits for readiness, runs the python poc client that performs the exact socket sequence above, then (crucially) uses `wait $SRV_PID` to propagate the server's own exit/signal status as run.sh's exit code so crash detection is unambiguous. Running the identical reproducer via run_poc against all three builds: post_intro -> exit=1, crashed=True, UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer reported "applying non-zero offset 8 to null pointer" in processMultibulkBuffer (networking.c:2516), immediately followed by an ASan abort ("nested bug in the same thread"), stack trace processMultibulkBuffer -> processInputBuffer -> readQueryFromClient -> connSocketEventHandler -> aeProcessEvents -> aeMain -> main -- exactly the argv-after-cron-free code path named in the bug/fix commit. pre_intro -> exit=0, crashed=False, server alive, SET returned "+OK\r\n" as expected. post_benign -> exit=0, crashed=False, server alive, SET returned "+OK\r\n" as expected. The same command/input was used across all three builds, satisfying the invariance requirement. This conclusively confirms introduction by the intro commit and resolution by the benign/fix commit.

oracle.description:
Python socket client connects to redis-server, sends only a multibulk header "*3
" (leaving c->argc==0 but c->multibulklen==3, i.e. the client is mid-command-parse), sleeps 3.5s so that clientsCronFreeArgvIfIdle (which only checked c->argc, not c->multibulklen) treats the client as idle and frees c->argv while resetting c->argv_len to 0, then sends the remainder of a SET command ("$3
SET
$3
key
$1
0
"). On fixed builds redis responds "+OK
" and stays alive; on the buggy intro build processMultibulkBuffer dereferences/offsets into the freed/NULL argv.
oracle.target_evidence: post_intro run_poc: exit=1 crashed=True. "networking.c:2516:17: runtime error: applying non-zero offset 8 to null pointer" in processMultibulkBuffer; "SUMMARY: UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer: undefined-behavior networking.c:2516:17"; "AddressSanitizer: nested bug in the same thread, aborting." pre_intro run_poc: exit=0 crashed=False; log shows "POC_RESULT: got response: b'+OK\\r\\n'", "POC_RESULT: OK_AS_EXPECTED", "SERVER_STILL_ALIVE". post_benign run_poc: exit=0 crashed=False; log shows "POC_RESULT: got response: b'+OK\\r\\n'", "POC_RESULT: OK_AS_EXPECTED", "SERVER_STILL_ALIVE".
